transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO - Archimedes), Liam O'Connor (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Reyes (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-gen): POC to validate Redwood inference for in-product summarization and structured extraction. Focus on OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function calling.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:11] Priya: Awesome. Quick agenda — scoping the POC, success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, and then integration considerations like our SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
[00:22] Sofia: That sounds right. We're most interested in latency for chat flows and reliable structured JSON output from tool calling.
[00:30] Liam: Also cost. We run a lot of short chats and some longer analysis requests; want to see per-token economics.
[00:36] Jordan: Totally. Maybe we start with success criteria — what would make this POC successful for you?
[00:42] Maya: For execs it's three things: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for short chat turns, 2) structured extraction accuracy above 92% on our validation set, and 3) predictable cost — ideally a 20% reduction vs our current vendor at target QPS.
[00:58] Priya: Helpful. When you say short chat turns, what's the average tokens per request?
[01:03] Liam: Avg prompt + user context is around 220 tokens, responses average 80 tokens. Peak concurrency is about 60 concurrent requests, sustained QPS around 25 — bursts to 75.
[01:14] Priya: Got it — that helps with workload sizing. For the POC we typically run a benchmark harness that mirrors those distributions. We'll test on our hosted offering first, then if you want run the same under Dedicated/reserved capacity to measure tail latency and cost predictability.
[01:28] Maya: Are your hosted endpoints OpenAI-compatible? Our dev team already builds against the OpenAI API surface.
[01:33] Jordan: Yes, we provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint surface in addition to our native SDKs. There might be occasional transcriptions of product names in logs — e.g., some places it's shown as "Red wood Dedicated" in transcripts — but the endpoints behave the same.
[01:46] Priya: We'll share sample code for both approaches — a drop-in OpenAI-compatible client, and a Redwood SDK that exposes advanced controls like automatic KV cache usage and batching.
[01:56] Liam: Can you do function/tool calling? We rely heavily on structured tool outputs to populate internal graphs.
[02:01] Priya: Yes, we support tool/function calling semantics and structured JSON outputs. We'll also show an example of enforced schema response so you can validate the extractor against your eval set.
[02:10] Sofia: Any limitations on streaming with function calls? We need streaming for UX snappiness.
[02:15] Priya: Streaming's supported; function call payloads can be streamed but you need to handle the final JSON assembly on the client. We'll include an example.
[02:23] Jordan: On benchmarks — our plan: week 1 is benchmark runs and baseline comparisons; week 2 is integration and eval. Does that timeline match your expectations?
[02:30] Maya: Yes, 2 weeks is fine. We can allocate engineering time.
[02:33] Liam: For the benchmark, what's the recommended setup?
[02:36] Priya: We generally ask for an anonymized test dataset and a manifest of request distributions. We'll run three types of tests: steady-state concurrency at your sustained QPS, burst testing to your peak, and long-context large-token runs to see KV cache behavior and memory pressure. We'll capture latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and per-token cost.
[02:53] Liam: For the large-token runs, we're talking sequences up to 6k tokens for some analysis tasks.
[02:58] Priya: We'll note that. Some infra tweaks help at that length — choice of model variant, quantization profiles, and kernel selection. We'll recommend model/quant settings after we see the dataset.
[03:08] Maya: Security questions — we need SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for keys, SSO/SAML, and audit logs.
[03:15] Jordan: We can share our security pack — SOC2 cert, KMS/HSM integration details, SSO options, and audit/log retention controls. We'll attach the docs.
[03:23] Sofia: On cost — are you able to show cost per 1k tokens for the different model families? We want a comparative table: hosted vs dedicated vs quantized variants.
[03:32] Priya: Yes, we'll provide an illustrative pricing matrix. For Dedicated, we'll show committed throughput economics; for Hosted, per-token rates. Keep in mind quantized variants will reduce compute cost but might affect accuracy slightly — we'll include quality-cost tradeoffs in the report.
[03:47] Liam: Regarding the OpenAI-compat endpoint, how seamless is moving from the OpenAI SDK? Any header/name changes?
[03:54] Priya: It's a drop-in — same endpoints and params for the most part. We also expose additional Redwood-specific headers for routing and debug traces. Some customers use the OpenAI-compatible surface for quick lift-and-shift, then migrate to Redwood SDK for fine-grained control.
[04:07] Jordan: We'll also include a sample serverless lambda snippet that shows how to stream responses and handle function-calling outputs.
[04:13] Maya: Great. For success criteria you mentioned accuracy thresholds — how do you recommend we evaluate that?
[04:18] Priya: Provide us a labeled validation set and the evaluation script you use (or we can run our own eval harness). We'll run OpenAI-compat and Redwood SDK pathways and produce a comparison table: extraction precision/recall, schema conformance, and failure modes.
[04:32] Liam: One operational question — do you do automatic prefix/KV caching? We want to reduce cost for repeated context.
[04:37] Priya: Yes, we have KV cache features; some of that is runtime behavior and some is configuration. It can be tuned per-route. Small caveat: transcriptions sometimes show "K V cash" and engineers laugh, but functionally it's KV cache and it helps with long-context efficiency.
[04:50] Sofia: Any suggested monitoring or observability we should add to our side?
[04:54] Priya: We recommend per-route token and latency metrics, plus tracing hooks on the client. Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, p95 latency, and error breakdowns. We'll also show how to set alerts for regressions in quality tied to specific prompt sets.
[05:08] Jordan: Let's lock down the exact benchmark metrics so we all agree. Proposed: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (rps), cost per 1k tokens, extraction F1 on validation set, and failure rate for function calls.
[05:19] Maya: That works. Can you also include a test for structured output schema conformance? If the model returns invalid JSON we need to count that as a failure.
[05:26] Priya: Absolutely. We'll add schema conformance and a count of malformed outputs as a metric.
[05:31] Liam: For the POC run — do you need network egress whitelisting or IP allowlist for the benchmark runners?
[05:36] Priya: For hosted benchmarks, no. If you prefer private connectivity we can run it in your VPC via our Private offering; that takes a bit longer to set up. For this POC we recommend hosted first to iterate quickly.
[05:50] Maya: If results look promising we'll consider Dedicated or Private. Our legal team will want an NDA add-on and a quick security review.
[05:57] Jordan: Noted. We'll send the SOC2 + security pack and a brief NDA template.
[06:02] Sofia: On integration, two quick asks: 1) sample code for OpenAI-compat and Redwood SDK, and 2) an example of function call schema enforcement and streaming.
[06:11] Priya: We'll deliver both. The SDK sample will show automatic batching knobs, KV cache hints, and a demo of structured output enforcement.
[06:19] Liam: For benchmarking, can Redwood also run the same tests under a quantized variant so we can compare cost/quality tradeoffs?
[06:24] Priya: Yep — we'll run the baseline model and a quantized variant; note that quantization tech varies by backend and may slightly change accuracy. We'll call out the model/quant names in the report.
[06:34] Jordan: Let's summarize next steps. Jordan to send pricing/arch/security pack; Priya to send SDK samples and benchmark harness; Archimedes to send dataset and QPS numbers; schedule bench run around 3/17. Any other items?
[06:49] Maya: That's it from me. One nuance — our compliance folks will want details on data retention for hosted logs; include retention TTL options.
[06:58] Jordan: Will include retention options.
[07:00] Sofia: When do you expect to have the initial benchmark report after the run?
[07:03] Priya: Usually 3 business days after the run to collate metrics and quality evals, so if run on 3/17 you'd have a report by 3/22.
[07:10] Liam: Sounds good.
[07:12] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:16] Maya: Thank you.

Recap / Close:
- POC length: 2 weeks (benchmark week + integration/eval week)
- Success criteria: p95 < 300ms for short chats, structured extraction accuracy >92%, cost target ~20% below current vendor at target QPS
- Benchmarks: steady-state QPS, peak bursts, long-context runs (up to 6k tokens), quantized variants, schema conformance checks
- Integration: OpenAI-compatible endpoint sample + Redwood SDK samples, function calling, streaming, KV cache hints
- Security: send SOC2, KMS details, SSO options, audit log retention options

References/Shared artifacts mentioned:
- "Redwood security pack (SOC2/KMS/SSO)" - link: (sent after call)
- "POC benchmark harness" - link: (will share)
- "SDK samples (python/node)" - link: (will share)

End of transcript.
